root_idea.summary: The root centers on one thing coming over, overtaking, or covering another, with a related branch involving haste, postponement, and the imposition of difficulty.
root_idea.development: The covering or overtaking principle extends to things befalling a person, causing hardship, and approaching or nearly catching up. A related usage concerns hastening or delaying until another time approaches.

senses.definition: To come upon, overtake, or overspread; to cover.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the subject is an affliction, darkness, humiliation, or comparable condition that overtakes and covers its object, especially the face or faces.

senses.definition: To cause a condition to come upon, overtake, or befall someone; to inflict it upon them.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses this causative construction for bringing excessive disobedience and disbelief upon people or causing those conditions to accompany them.

senses.definition: To impose a difficult or arduous thing on someone; to burden or overburden them.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction may describe making a person bear hardship or difficulty, including an arduous task or a demand that is hard to endure.

senses.definition: Wrongdoing, injustice, or oppressive conduct; the doing of what is forbidden.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the directly attested moral reading of the Quranic noun, particularly in the expression concerning neither loss nor wrongdoing. Related interpretive explanations include sin, error, bad conduct, or pride.

senses.definition: An affliction or burdensome harm that overtakes someone.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied contextual rendering of one Quranic occurrence is “burden.” The lexical evidence supports an overtaking or affliction branch, but does not settle every exegetical nuance; related reported interpretations include weakness, lowness, or ruin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach, come near, reach, or overtake a person or thing; to come upon an event, debt, or appointed time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be reached without necessarily being seized; the expression can also describe following until one is nearly caught.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inflict on someone something disliked or hateful.
To be regarded as affected by rahq; to be suspected of evil conduct or religious impropriety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive characterization of a person, including being considered ignorant or morally suspect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach puberty or virility; to nearly attain a specified age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a boy approaching sexual maturity and also of nearly reaching an age such as twenty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause pursuers or riders to catch up with, overtake, or nearly overtake someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used causatively of making horsemen or another pursuer come up with the pursued party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge or incite someone to do what is beyond his ability to bear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a broader causative use involving an excessive or unmanageable demand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To delay a prayer until the time of the next prayer approaches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional temporal expression; the delay may be described as continuing until the next appointed time is near.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hurry someone in a way that prevents or deters him from praying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized causative construction concerning being hurried away from prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rashness, haste, levity, foolishness, or ignorance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These characterize a person’s conduct or disposition rather than the Quranic noun’s directly attested moral construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ill nature, lying, or a proud and self-conceited disposition.
A person characterized by quickness to evil, moral recklessness, or haughtiness; رَهِقَةٌ can refer to a vicious or adulterous woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form has the explicitly reported application to a woman of vicious or adulterous conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run so fast that one’s pursuer must attempt something difficult or beyond his power, or so that the pursued person is nearly overtaken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression describing extreme speed in pursuit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: As many as a hundred, especially a company of people or a group of camels.
A wide-stepping, swift, or excellent she-camel that nearly treads on the person leading her.
A boy or girl from approximately ten to eleven years of age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The masculine and feminine forms are applied respectively to a boy and a girl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saffron.
Reached or overtaken, especially to the point of being caught and slain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive participial description of one who has been caught by a pursuer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Straitened or placed under oppressive difficulty.
The time at which the afternoon prayer is drawing near.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical temporal expression referring to the approach of prayer time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person to whom people frequently come and at whose abode guests alight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can describe a hospitable person whose dwelling is often visited.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person suspected of evil, ignorance, corrupt conduct, or religious impropriety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the passive characterization of one to whom rahq is attributed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near to attaining puberty; an adolescent approaching sexual maturity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a boy, with the feminine form used for a girl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearly at the end of an appointed or proper time, so that the opportunity is almost missed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of entering a place nearly too late for the relevant pilgrimage rite or performing a prayer nearly after its proper time.

cautions: The noun رَهَقٌ has several reported interpretive readings in the Quranic material, including wrongdoing, affliction, suspicion, weakness, and ruin; the supplied evidence does not assign each alternative to a distinct modern verse location.
Lane’s historical Quran citation notation has not been converted into modern verse locations; Quran examples use only independently supplied QAC locations.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: For رَهَقًا at 72:6, the contextual gloss “burden” is compatible with the lexical affliction/overtaking branch, but the supplied Lane and Mufradat material does not resolve the full exegetical interpretation.
